title: Covariant Path Integrals and Observation Regularity on Physical--Observation State Spaces
content: The physical--observation dual-axis (PODA) structure treats physical and observation configurations as distinct arguments of joint dynamics. We study the analytic conditions under which this structure admits rigorous path integrals and finite complex measures for sequential quantum histories. On compact smooth joint geometry, a specified covariant Hamiltonian has a Feynman--Kac representation. A uniform complex-time product estimate permits simultaneous removal of Abel damping and time slicing at arbitrary relative speeds. For fixed finite bounded-readout protocols, class operators converge strongly and the trace-class branch-pair operators converge in trace norm. Finite instruments with complete Kraus families also yield trace-norm convergence of their record states. Energy-form regularity gives quantitative error bounds. A completed cylinder-test space carries a consistent, strongly positive history functional. The stronger finite-measure question is controlled by covariant transport: calibrated rank-one readouts on a finite-dimensional fibre satisfy the sharp estimate \( \|\mu_\gamma\|_{TV}\leq e^{2c_\gamma} \), where \( c_\gamma \) is the off-diagonal covariant variation. In the specified common-action class, conserved energy and smooth, globally labelled rank-one readouts imply this regularity when the kinetic geometry is complete and the effective potential is bounded below, or when the chosen energy confines the trajectory to a compact set. In infinite dimension, finitely many readout sectors allow unbounded internal energies and bounded transitions. The construction extends to countable outcomes when the operator of block norms is bounded on \( \ell^2 \); nonatomic readouts admit a double-Dyson construction when an absolute integral kernel is bounded on \( L^2 \). In these Dyson constructions, pure preparations with rank-one discrete readouts or scalar continuous fibres have exact variation \( \|e^{T\mathsf B}v\|_2^2 \). Whole-sector and spatial-domain cutoffs converge in variation, whereas nonatomic readout quantization converges weakly and remains separated in variation norm. Mixed curvature survives in the covariant constructions, and invariant quantum embeddings recover physical-sector histories. Unrestricted basis switching, a bounded-Hamiltonian countable example and free-particle position histories establish the limits of finite-measure existence; exact physical recovery transfers the last obstruction to the joint theory. Analytic two-axis models exhibit the resulting dynamics and verify the distinct convergence statements. A proposed two-mode trapped-ion realization links the magnetic oscillator's transport phase to independent spectral and driven-response tests. Exact finite-time Gaussian evolution shows that nearly complete wave-packet return can coexist with a substantial phase correction. The protocol therefore infers the coupling from finite-time interference and predicts the other observables without refitting, with calibration and uncertainty requirements explicit. These are model predictions, not measured data. Each construction is tied to its stated geometric, dynamical and readout hypotheses.
